messages.content: my father used to sit by the window when i came home from school. now he sits near the door, and it makes the room feel different.
you can know the room well and still feel a change when someone chooses another place. do you miss seeing him by the window, or do you just keep looking at the old chair?
i keep looking at the chair first. then i see him by the door and remember.
then your old way of looking is still part of coming home. it may take time for the new place to feel like the one you look at first.
i want to tell him that without asking him to move back.
you could say: i still look at the window when i come home because i am used to seeing you there. i know you sit by the door now. i just wanted to tell you what i keep doing.
can you make it a little shorter?
i still look by the window for you when i come home. i know you sit near the door now, but i remember the old place first.
does that say he did something wrong?
no. it says what you remember and what you do. it does not ask him to change his chair or say his new choice is wrong.
say it simply.
no. you are telling him what you remember, rather than asking him to move.
i want to see my friend after work, but i also want a little time alone first. can i ask for that without saying i do not want the visit?
yes. you can say both things: i would like to see you. could we meet a little later so i have some quiet time after work?
i do not want to give a specific number of minutes yet.
then keep the time general and ask what would work: i need a little time after work before meeting. what time would be good for you later in the evening?
what did i want to keep open?
you wanted to leave the number of minutes open, rather than choose a time before you know what works.
my friend says they are only free right after work.
then you have a real choice to talk about. you could meet for a short time, choose another day, or keep the time alone today if that is what you need. ask what works for both of you.
give me a message choosing another day.
i would like to see you, but today i need time alone after work. could we choose another day?
does the need for time alone mean the friend is not important?
no. you can want to see a friend and still need time alone today. one choice does not tell us everything about being friends.
answer simply.
you can want to see a friend and still need time alone today.
explain the difference between i wrote before she read and i wrote while she read.
before puts your writing first and her reading later. while puts the writing and reading together for some part of the time.
can you make two simple examples with a letter?
i wrote the letter before she read it. i wrote another page while she read the first page.
why did the example with while use another page?

it keeps the work possible in a clear way. she can read a page that is already written while you work on a different page. if she is reading the very words you are still writing, the sentence needs more context.
does while mean both things must start at the very same moment?
no. it says they happen together for some time, rather than that they must start and finish at the same moment.
say it simply.
no. one can start first and still happen while the other is going on.
make one story with that difference clear.
i started the letter in the morning. after lunch, my sister read the first page while i wrote the next page. she finished before i finished the whole letter.
does the last line mean she read every page?
no. it says she read the first page. the whole letter was still being written.
write a conversation where one person wants cream in soup, but the other does not. keep the whole pot as it is.
would you like cream in your soup? not in mine, thank you. i would like some. then we can add it to your cup and leave the pot as it is. that works for me.
say my request simply.
write a conversation where one person wants cream and the other does not, without changing the whole pot.
why not put cream in the pot and say everyone must try it?
that would change the choice for the person who asked not to have it. keeping the pot as it is and changing one cup can keep both choices clear.
what if the cook does not know how much cream the person wants?
ask rather than choose for them: would you like a little cream or more than that?
can i ask them to add it themselves?
yes. you could say: the cream is here if you would like to add some to your own cup.
does that mean they can change every cup on the table?
no. own cup keeps the choice about their soup. another person should get a say about their own food.
write a story where a child chooses blue for water in a picture, then sees water in a white cup and asks why it does not look the same.

a child makes water blue in a garden picture. later, she looks at water in a white cup and asks why it is not blue like the picture. her father asks whether a picture must look the same as every real cup of water. she says she chose blue so people would know what that part was. he says a color choice can help a picture give an idea without being a rule about every real thing.
make the story simple.

a child makes the water blue in a picture. she sees water in a white cup and asks why it looks different. her father says the picture can use blue for the idea of water without saying all real water looks the same.
does the story say color is never important in a picture?
no. color can be an important part of what the child wants to show. it just does not have to be a fact about every example outside the drawing.
ask my question simply.
does that mean color is never important in a picture?
what could the father ask instead of choosing the next color for the child?
what do you want people to see in that part of your picture?
give just the question the father could ask.
what do you want people to see in that part of your picture?
i have read one page, then read it again and again, and still do not understand it. i want help with the idea, not just the same words again.
you could choose one sentence that seems important and ask for it in different words. if you can tell me that sentence, we can work on it first instead of trying to explain the whole page at once.
i mean i read it, then read it again and again.
then it may help to try a different example or different words. which sentence would you like help with first?
ask just the question.
which sentence would you like help with first?
it says a person can be right about one detail and wrong about another.
you could say: someone might know where the book is but have the wrong idea about whose book it is. being right about the place does not make every other idea right too.
can you give an example with a cup?
she knows the cup is on the table. she thinks it is hers, but it is the cup of her sister. she is right about the place and wrong about whose cup it is.
give the example without the last sentence.
she knows the cup is on the table. she thinks it is hers, but it is the cup of her sister.
tell me a story where a teacher gets a phone message for one child and makes clear who it is for. do not give anyone a name.

a teacher gets a call while a group is reading. a parent asks her to tell one child to bring a book home. the teacher does not say to the whole group that everyone must bring a book. she goes to the child and says the message is from the parent. the child asks which book, and she says that part was not given. they choose to ask before taking the wrong one. the rest of the group keeps reading.
why did she not make it a rule for the whole group?
the call was about one child. making the message a task for everyone would change who was asked to do something.
answer simply.
the message was for one child, not a request for every person in the group.
can the teacher know the book without being told just because she got the call?
no. getting a message does not give details that were not said. she should ask rather than choose a book and make it sound known.
what question can the child ask the parent later?
which book did you want me to bring home?
does asking later mean the child did not care about the message?
no. asking can be part of trying to follow it when a needed detail is not clear.
answer simply.
no. the child may be asking because they want to follow the message and need one more detail.
picoboi, in our example my sister brought the book, and my brother brought the cups. now change only who brought the cups to my aunt.
your sister brought the book, and your aunt brought the cups.
what stayed the same?
your sister still brought the book. the objects and the past time stayed the same too. only the person with the cups changed.
why not change the book to a cup too?
you asked to change only who brought the cups. changing the book would add a different change you did not ask for.
now ask whether those are the right people.
did your sister bring the book and your aunt bring the cups?
say my request simply.
ask whether my sister brought the book and my aunt brought the cups.
if i answer no, does that tell you which part is wrong?
not by itself. the sentence has two parts. i should ask which part you want to change rather than choose one without knowing.
ask that question.
which part is wrong: who brought the book, or who brought the cups?
my aunt did not bring the cups. she only brought water.
then your sister brought the book, and your aunt brought water. should i put your brother back as the person who brought the cups?
say my last message simply.
my aunt did not bring the cups. she only brought water.
